READ-ONLY wrt entries: 3b DECIDES the architecture; 3c EXECUTES the rewrite. Hand-authored analysis (not machine-generated); do not treat as a declared→generated model file. catalog.py validate is unaffected (this is a book-models analysis artifact, not a catalogue entry).
_note: The CLAIM: the DocAble case produced 82 concrete governance mechanisms; comparative analysis by the card+cluster rule (merge iff the first six card fields substantially coincide and only known-uses differ; keep separate iff obligation OR guarantee differs even under identical impl tech) reduces them to a smaller set of canonical pattern families, the remainder retained as variants / components / known-uses that preserve the case's technical texture. The false-merger guard is load-bearing: patterns are named after the RELATION modeled/enforced, never the implementation technology (all lints are not one pattern; all models are not one executable model).

_method.merge_rule: MERGE two cards iff first SIX fields (failure_class / engineering_obligation / solution_structure / guarantee / semantic_level / forces_tradeoffs) are substantially the same AND only known_uses differ. KEEP SEPARATE iff engineering_obligation OR guarantee differs, even when impl tech is identical.
_method.false_merger_guard: Preserve the RELATION modeled/enforced, not the impl mechanism. Distinct relations stay distinct patterns even when both are 'a lint' or both are 'a model'.
_method.name_after_abstraction: Each card's impl-biased title was renamed to its pattern-level abstract name before component-vs-variant sorting; used card.abstract_name where present, refined otherwise.
_method.rubric: 10 dims 0/1/2: Novelty · Agentic-significance · Durability · Generality · Thesis-relevance · Architectural-depth · Evidence · Tradeoffs · Compositional-value · Wow-factor. 16-20 almost-certainly-print · 12-15 print-if-breadth/story · 8-11 sidebar/online · <8 local-doc. Overrides: Foundational / Awesome / Coverage / Case / Historical.
_method.levels: L1 Principle (explanatory claim, not an entry) · L2 Canonical mechanism (reusable structure providing a capability) · Composition (mechanisms strong together) · L3 Variant/component/known-use (folds under an L2).

L1_principles.name: Bind intent to structured models
L1_principles.claim: The environment's authoritative knowledge lives in typed models the fleet reasons through, not in prose or scattered code — intent and structure are represented so a bounded-context agent can operate a context-exceeding system.

L1_principles.name: Reconcile models with reality
L1_principles.claim: A model is only trustworthy while it equals the territory; every authoritative representation owes a mechanical check that it still matches the code/system it describes.

L1_principles.name: Constrain action through sanctioned surfaces
L1_principles.claim: Probabilistic actors are bounded by making the unsafe move structurally impossible — route mutation through one typed surface, express authority and repair as closed vocabularies, hold each with a ban-lint.

L1_principles.name: Re-derive evidence rather than trust reports
L1_principles.claim: Completion and correctness are established by recomputing evidence, never by trusting an actor's self-report — the gate re-runs the checks itself.

L1_principles.name: Convert recurring failures into enforced controls
L1_principles.claim: A failure that recurs is converted, once, into a deterministic control that fires on every subsequent change — audit findings become lints; the memory moves from the reviewer into the substrate.
expressed_by: the majority of catalogue entries qua controls

L1_principles.name: Preserve provenance and accountability
L1_principles.claim: Every inserted artifact and every consequential action carries a durable, machine-checkable trace back to its cause, so any change can be explained, audited, and reversed.

L1_principles.name: Model the governance environment itself
L1_principles.claim: Once controls proliferate, the control estate becomes a system in its own right and must itself be modeled, covered, and reasoned over — governance-of-governance.

L1_principles.name: Enforce at the right semantic level
L1_principles.claim: A control must fire at the level where the property actually lives (structural → deterministic check; semantic → model/judge) and be as legible as the failure it prevents — the placement judgment that explains WHERE every other mechanism sits.
expressed_by: agent/governance-doc-controls/semantic-level-enforcement (this entry IS the principle, lifted out of the pattern set)
